title: Emergent Surface Kondo Flat Band Driven by Competing Interactions in a Topological Ferromagnet
authors: Nazar Zaremba, Susmita Changdar, Haojie Guo, Iñigo Robredo, Daniel Lozano-Gomez, Andreas Leithe-Jasper, Rui Lou, Yurii Prots, Mitja Krnel, Markus König, Konstantin Semeniuk, Berit H. Goodge, Yuri Grin, Andrii Kuibarov, Oleksandr Suvorov, Alexander Fedorov, Adam Pikul, Ivan Soldatov, Rudolf Schäfer, Bernd Büchner, Oksana Kvitnitskaya, Yurii Naidyuk, Louis Lamm, Meike Pfeiffer, Elena Hassinger, Matthias Vojta, Sergey Borisenko, Miguel M. Ugeda, Jeroen van den Brink, Eteri Svanidze, Maia G. Vergniory
abstract: A central goal of modern condensed matter physics is to uncover new quantum states of matter arising from the intertwined effects of strong electron correlations, magnetism, and band topology. Heavy-fermion phases, generated by Kondo interactions, represent one of the most remarkable manifestations of electronic correlations, and topological heavy-fermion states have been identified in several non-magnetic materials. Yet, the consequences of their competition with magnetic order have remained largely unexplored. Here, we reveal a new phenomenon: the spontaneous spatial separation of correlated quantum phases. By showing that magnetism can drive distinct strongly correlated electronic states to coexist in different regions of a single material, our work establishes a previously unknown mechanism for organizing quantum matter and opens a new direction in the study of correlated topological systems. Using \emph{bulk-sensitive} probes, we show that UAsS crystals are, in the bulk, metallic ferromagnets with only moderate correlation-driven band renormalizations. First-principles calculations reveal a topological electronic structure hosting both nodal lines and Weyl points, pointing to a rich underlying topology. Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) measurements are consistent with these predictions, resolving the nodal lines and Weyl crossings. In striking contrast, \emph{surface-sensitive} ARPES and scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy (STM/STS) measurements reveal a pronounced flat band pinned at the Fermi level, accompanied by a sharp resonance -- hallmarks of an emergent, strongly correlated Kondo state not captured by first-principles calculations.
summary: This research investigates the interplay between magnetism, topology, and strong correlations in UAsS, finding that the material exhibits a bulk topological ferromagnetism. Crucially, surface measurements reveal an emergent, strongly correlated Kondo flat band, demonstrating a mechanism where competing interactions drive distinct quantum phases to coexist spatially within one crystal.
main_problem: The central goal is to understand quantum states arising from the competition between strong electron correlations (Kondo interactions), magnetism, and band topology in correlated materials.
main_result: The work reveals a novel phenomenon of spontaneous spatial separation of correlated quantum phases, where the surface exhibits a strongly correlated Kondo state distinct from the bulk ferromagnetic topological state.
method: The study combines first-principles calculations (DFT), advanced spectroscopic measurements (ARPES, STM/STS), and theoretical modeling using mean-field theory for Hamiltonian analysis.
model_or_system: The primary system is UAsS, a topological ferromagnet based on 5f electrons. Theoretical models involve analyzing the competition between Kondo and Heisenberg interactions in lattice models.
key_observables: Flat band pinned at the Fermi level (surface), nodal lines and Weyl points (bulk), Zero Bias Anomaly (ZBA) width, and spatial dependence of mean-field parameters.
important_parameters: Kondo temperature ($T_K \sim 52 	ext{ K}$), Curie temperature ($T_C = 126 	ext{ K}$), and coupling strengths ($J_K, J$).
main_assumptions: The surface Kondo state is assumed to be emergent and not captured by bulk DFT; the ZBA analysis relies on fitting to Fermi liquid theory for Kondo resonance.
figures_summary: Figures show bulk ferromagnetism and topological features (nodal lines); surface probes reveal the flat band; theoretical figures map the spatial variation of electronic structure and correlation parameters.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the theoretical context of competing interactions, presenting experimental evidence showing bulk ferromagnetism alongside surface Kondo resonances, and finally using theoretical models to confirm the mechanism of spatial phase separation.
why_interesting: The concept of spatially separated correlated phases—where surface physics deviates fundamentally from bulk predictions due to competing interactions—is highly relevant for understanding interface effects in quantum materials.
